## What's new

Threadnote 5.0.0 turns working context into a verifiable lifecycle across agents, from reviewed closeout to health checks, CI, procedures, and private value reports.

### Agent integration catalog

`threadnote agents list --json` now reports a catalog of 27 agent surfaces with setup guidance, capability boundaries,
platform coverage, and verification metadata. Managed integrations can be previewed, installed, repaired, inspected, and
removed through one lifecycle. New managed user-scope paths include Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Amp, and Factory Droid;
catalog-only and partial entries stay clearly marked instead of being presented as fully managed.

### Lifecycle and closeout foundations

Memory schema v5 adds optional ownership and `review_after` maintenance metadata. Bounded Knowledge Deltas and
`threadnote closeout preview/apply` make proposed context changes reviewable before they become durable knowledge.

`threadnote context health` reports stale citations, review dates, broken relations, duplicates, and pending conflicts in
text or JSON without mutating memory. `threadnote context check` scopes those findings to changed files and provides stable
text, JSON, and SARIF results for CI.

### Verified procedures and private value reports

Procedure manifests can be verified against exact artifacts and fixtures, then inspected as current, incompatible,
locally modified, unverified, or update-available. Verification is preview-first and never executes downloaded procedures
automatically.

`threadnote value report` summarizes the local task-context loop using content-free counts. Its explicit export remains
preview-first and redacted: it excludes queries, memory text, source code, paths, repository names, and stable user IDs.
